It elaborates the Mu Tianzi template into a full revelation scene: ranking of immortals, dietetics, sexual continence warnings, and the emperor's failure to fully cultivate. Widely cited in Daoist bibliographies as a classic of 'inner biography' (內傳) genre.
entries.key_passages: 王母曰：夫欲修身，當愛氣養神，服食草木，則可延年；若能得道，則升天矣。
entries.application: Illustrates graded transmission and the contingency of destiny on practice—used in cultivation ethics and discussions of imperial vs. true immortal fate.
entries.related: 穆天子傳; 漢武故事; 茅君內傳

entries.deep_essence: A doctrinal summa of Lingbao/Dongxuan teachings (Daozang CT 1124), expounding the 'great meanings of the Mysterious Gate'—cosmology, the Three Caverns, ranks of scriptures, body-spirit correspondence, and soteriological paths. Likely Tang or earlier medieval scholastic composition used for clerical education. It systematizes Lingbao metaphysics: qi transformations, the role of zhai retreats, and the unity of Dao, scriptures, and master (道經師).
entries.key_passages: 玄門大義者，所以明道體、辯教相、通科儀、示修行之路也。
entries.application: Provides the metaphysical map (Three Treasures, qi phases) against which BaZi five-phase analysis and Daoist destiny theory are calibrated.
entries.related: 道教義樞; 雲笈七籤; 洞玄靈寶三洞奉道科戒營始

entries.deep_essence: A disciplinary and ritual-protocol text (Daozang CT 1126) for Lingbao 'Dao-learning' (道學): rules for ordinands, daily observances, scriptural recitation schedules, pure chamber conduct, and hierarchical etiquette. It functions as a medieval clerical handbook combining precepts (科) with ceremonial forms (儀). Scholars use it to reconstruct Tang–Song Daoist education and the institutional framing of cultivation.
entries.key_passages: 凡入道學者，當先持戒行，次習經法，後行科教。
entries.application: Structures daily/seasonal practice routines that align with calendrical stems and branches—practical scaffolding for long-term BaZi-informed cultivation.
entries.related: 三洞奉道科戒營始; 玄門十事威儀; 正一威儀經

entries.name_han: 北帝七元紫庭延生祕訣
entries.deep_essence: An esoteric Northern Emperor (北帝) / Dipper (七元) longevity manual (Daozang-related Beidi corpus). It teaches invocations of the seven star lords of the Northern Dipper (北斗七元), Purple Court (紫庭) visualization, and methods to extend life, dissolve calamities, and petition destiny offices. Part of the Tang–Song Beidi and Doumu liturgical stream that fused exorcism, star magic, and life-extension rites.
entries.key_passages: 北斗七元，主人生死罪福；禮斗延生，可以消災度厄，增福延壽。
entries.application: Directly relevant to BaZi: Dipper lords govern lifespan and misfortune; dou rituals are classic chart-remediation and yan sheng (延生) methods.
entries.related: 太上玄靈北斗本命延生真經; 北斗七元金玄羽章; 北帝伏魔經

entries.deep_essence: A short Zhengyi text framed as Celestial Master Zhang Daoling's oral secrets to disciple Zhao Sheng (趙昇), one of the legendary three who passed the master's trials. Content typically covers covenant oaths, register (籙) empowerment logic, exorcistic formulas, and the ethics of transmitting Zhengyi methods. It belongs to the Celestial Masters hagiographic-instruction genre preserving early Tianshi self-understanding of lineage authentication.
entries.key_passages: 吾將去矣，授汝要訣，慎勿輕傳；非盟誓不得妄示。
entries.application: Models legitimate transmission and oath-bound practice; BaZi masters in Zhengyi lines invoke similar covenantal structure when teaching destiny arts.
entries.related: 正一法文天師教戒科經; 張天師二十四治圖; 老君音誦誡經

entries.deep_essence: A Dongshen (洞神, Cavern of Spirit) ordination and 'walking the Dao' (行道) investiture liturgy (Daozang ritual corpus). It specifies altar layout, scriptural titles conferred, registers delivered, and sequential rites for initiating practitioners into the Dongshen canon—historically associated with the Sanhuang (三皇) and related talismanic traditions. Essential for reconstructing the Three Caverns ordination ladder below Dongzhen and Dongxuan.
entries.key_passages: 行道授度，當依科啟師，陳詞立誓，授以經籙，方得行持。
entries.application: Ordination calendars and auspicious-hour selection for授度 connect ritual time to sexagenary computation used in BaZi.
entries.related: 太上洞神三皇儀; 傳授經戒儀注訣; 洞神八帝妙精經

entries.deep_essence: The literary-philosophical collected works of Zhang Yuchu (張宇初, 1361–1410), 43rd Celestial Master of the Zhengyi order, titled 《峴泉集》. Includes prefaces, essays on Daoist doctrine, Neidan reflections, institutional reforms under early Ming, and defenses of Zhengyi liturgical identity versus Quanzhen. A primary source for late imperial Celestial Master intellectual history and the synthesis of inner alchemy with communal ritual.
entries.key_passages: 道貴清靜，法貴正一；內修性命，外濟幽顯。
entries.application: Articulates Ming Zhengyi balance of inner cultivation and public rites—context for how BaZi and liturgical destiny work coexisted in Celestial Master institutions.
entries.related: 道門十規; 漢天師世家; 龍虎山志

entries.deep_essence: A Lingbao 'food-bestowal' (施食) method for feeding hungry ghosts and orphaned souls, parallel to Buddhist ullambana/yoga-flaming-mouth rites but using Lingbao talismans, mudras, and mantric formulas. Manuals in the Daozang and later Zhengyi collections detail altar setup, transformation of food through qi and true writs, and dedication of merit. Core of evening salvation liturgies (晚朝/普度).
entries.key_passages: 以靈寶法食，普施河沙餓鬼，令得飽滿，離苦升真。
entries.application: Ritual care of deceased kin and hungry ghosts supports ancestral-luck dimensions of BaZi; timing often set by lunar and sexagenary days.
entries.related: 靈寶領教濟度金書; 薩祖鐵罐施食; 黃籙破獄燈儀

entries.deep_essence: A Tang-period yangsheng (養生) treatise by Liu Ci (劉詞), also titled 《混俗頤生錄》, advising how to nourish life while living 'mixed in the vulgar world' (混俗). Covers diet, sleep, sexual moderation, seasonal regimen, emotional hygiene, and mild herbal support without full withdrawal to the mountains. Represents elite lay longevity culture between pure immortality quest and ordinary household life; preserved in medical-Daoist collectanea.
entries.key_passages: 混俗而不染，頤生而不貪；四時調攝，可盡天年。
entries.application: Seasonal and daily regimen advice maps onto BaZi strength/weakness of day-master: supporting deficient phases through lifestyle.
entries.related: 養性延命錄; 保生要錄; 孫真人攝養論

entries.deep_essence: A concise Song yangsheng handbook attributed to Pu Qia (蒲虔貫), 《保生要錄》, summarizing essentials for preserving life: regulating the four seasons, dietetics, massage, breath practice, and avoiding depleting activities. Frequently anthologized with other short medical-Daoist pamphlets; practical rather than mystical, aimed at officials and literati seeking longevity without intensive Neidan.
entries.key_passages: 保生之道，莫先於養氣；養氣之要，在於慎起居、節飲食、遠房室。
entries.application: Operational health rules that complement BaZi yearly luck analysis—adjusting diet and activity by season and personal phase balance.
entries.related: 混俗頤生錄; 頤生微論; 修真祕錄

entries.deep_essence: A yangsheng/Neidan-adjacent 'secret record of cultivating perfection' associated with Fu Du (傅度) or related Tang–Song compilers (editions vary in catalogues). It collects methods for refining the body-spirit: breathing, dietary avoidance, minor elixir tips, and warnings about leakage of essence. Sits on the continuum between medical nourishing-life texts and early internal alchemy; often cited in Daoist bibliographic notes as a practical xiuzhen digest.
entries.key_passages: 修真之要，在閉精養氣，守神反聽，久則神全氣固。
entries.application: Essence conservation and seasonal practice reinforce BaZi counsel on protecting weak water/wood or controlling excessive fire/metal.
entries.related: 修真歷驗鈔圖; 保生要錄; 坐忘論

entries.deep_essence: A illustrated seasonal yangsheng work (four-qi life-regulating charts), traditionally linked to Tang graphic-medical culture and later printed editions. It depicts how the four seasonal qi (spring birth, summer growth, autumn harvest, winter storage) should guide diet, exercise, sleeping posture, and emotional stance. The '圖' format made it a teaching aid; content aligns with Huangdi Neijing seasonal philosophy filtered through Daoist regimen schools.
entries.key_passages: 春生夏長，秋收冬藏；逆之則災害生，從之則苛疾不起。
entries.application: Direct template for calendrical self-care used with BaZi month branches and annual luck (流年) phase advice.
entries.related: 黃帝內經素問·四氣調神大論; 混俗頤生錄; 保生要錄

entries.deep_essence: A technical esoteric tract on cultivating numinous mushrooms (芝), preserved in Daoist and fangshi literature (variants in Yunji Qiqian and pharmaceutical collections). It describes soil selection, timing by lunar mansions and sexagenary days, ritual purity when planting or harvesting lingzhi, and the ranking of zhi types as immortality foods. Reflects early medieval herb-magic (仙藥) culture linking agriculture of numina to transcendence.
entries.key_passages: 種芝當擇名山福地，以甲子日下種，齋戒潔淨，可獲靈芝。
entries.application: Herb-gathering and planting days require stem-branch selection—classic applied calendrics shared with BaZi date selection (擇日).
entries.related: 抱朴子內篇·仙藥; 太上靈寶芝草品; 神仙服餌丹石行藥法
